Cobalt. Co.

A metal known to Hohenheim in the fourteenth century. Derives its name
from the German word Kobold, signifying mischievous spirit, so named by the
miners who considered it a profitless ore. It is found in conjunction with nickel
from which it has to be separated, a process first taught in 1807 by a chemist

phia chemist, who produced absolutely pure Kobalt in 1850.

From this chemically pure Kobalt Hering made his proving in July, 1850.

Further provings were made by Koller, Lippe, Jones and Sparhawk. See
Allen's Encyclopedia, vol. 5, p. 361.
